name: MKL02Z32VFK4R
title: Kinetis KL02 48 MHz Cortex-M0+ microcontroller, up to 32 KB flash, 16/24/32-pin QFN
summary: The KL02 is a small 32-bit microcontroller on an ARM Cortex-M0+ core clocked up to 48 MHz, with up to 32 KB of flash and 4 KB of SRAM, sold in 3 mm, 4 mm and 5 mm QFN packages with 16, 24 or 32 pins. It runs from 1.71 V to 3.6 V (flash writes included) over -40 °C to 105 °C ambient, and has nine low-power modes, down to a few hundred nanoamps in VLLS0. On chip: a 12-bit SAR ADC, an analog comparator with a 6-bit DAC, two 2-channel TPM timers, a 16-bit low-power timer, one SPI, one low-power UART and two I2C modules. MKL02Z32VFK4R is the 32 KB part in the 24-pin QFN on tape and reel.
key_figures: up to 32 KB / up to 4 KB
4.26 mA typ, 48 MHz, peripheral clocks off, 3.0 V
down to 2 µA with full state retention, 4 µs wake-up

notes: A trailing R on the part number (packaging field N) orders tape and reel; no suffix orders trays. M: fully qualified; V: -40 °C to 105 °C; 4: 48 MHz.

operation.text: A Cortex-M0+ core runs at up to 48 MHz with zero-wait-state flash, a bit manipulation engine and a Micro Trace Buffer, built on a 90 nm TFS process. Flash is 8, 16 or 32 KB and SRAM 1, 2 or 4 KB by part. Each chip carries an 80-bit unique ID. Debug is over SWD. A COP watchdog is included. Throughput is up to 15.9 CoreMark/mA (CoreMark 1.0, IAR ARM 6.50.2, code in flash, data in RAM, 48 MHz, 3.3 V).

12-bit SAR ADC; analog comparator (CMP) with a 6-bit DAC and selectable reference input; two 2-channel TPM timer/PWM modules; a 16-bit low-power timer (LPTMR); one 8-bit SPI; one low-power UART; two I2C modules; up to 28 GPIO.

The 32-pin QFN brings VDD, VREFH, VREFL and VSS out on four pins. In the 24-pin and 16-pin QFN, VDD and VREFH share one pin and VREFL and VSS share another. VDDA tracks VDD within ±0.1 V and VSSA tracks VSS within ±0.1 V. On packages without separate reference pins, VREFH is tied inside to VDDA and VREFL to VSSA. RAM keeps its contents down to VDD = 1.2 V.

POR trips on falling VDD between 0.8 V and 1.5 V. The low-voltage detector has a high range (2.56 V typ) and a low range (1.60 V typ), each with four warning levels set by LVWV. tPOR, from VDD reaching 1.8 V to the first instruction, is at most 300 µs with normal boot.

The chip has nine low-power modes; currents are given for WAIT, STOP, partial stop 2, VLPR, VLPW, VLPS and the very-low-leakage stops VLLS3, VLLS1 and VLLS0. Waking from VLPS or STOP takes 4 µs typ; from VLLS3 42 µs; from VLLS1 93 µs; from VLLS0 95 µs. In VLPR and VLPS the core clock is limited to 4 MHz and the bus and flash clocks to 1 MHz, overriding any other module's figure. Recovery from POR and VLLSx starts in FEI at 21 MHz.

Each I/O pad has an ESD clamp to VSS but none to VDD. PTA12, PTA13, PTB0 and PTB1 can be set to high drive (20 mA at VDD ≥ 2.7 V with VOH ≥ VDD - 0.5 V); every other GPIO is normal drive (VOH ≥ VDD - 0.5 V at 5 mA, VDD ≥ 2.7 V). Total output current for all ports is limited to 100 mA sourcing and 100 mA sinking. Internal pull-ups are 20 kΩ to 50 kΩ. PTB3 and PTB4 are true open drain and need external pull-ups. The RESET pin carries only an active pull-down, and as a GPIO output it is pseudo open drain. After reset most port pins are disabled; PTA0 comes up as SWD_CLK, PTA2 as SWD_DIO, PTA1 as RESET_b, PTB5 as NMI_b, PTA3/PTA4 as EXTAL0/XTAL0, and several pins as ADC inputs.

The MCG has a 32.768 kHz slow internal reference and a 4 MHz fast internal reference, and an FLL whose DCO runs 20 MHz to 48 MHz; a 1 kHz LPO clock is also on chip. The crystal oscillator takes 32 kHz to 40 kHz crystals or resonators, in low-power mode (HGO = 0, 500 nA, internal feedback resistor) or high-gain mode (HGO = 1, 25 µA, 10 MΩ feedback and 200 kΩ series resistor). Load capacitors Cx and Cy can be the on-chip ones or external parts, valued per the crystal vendor's recommendation; in low-power mode no external feedback resistor is fitted. EXTAL and XTAL connect only to the oscillator components. An external clock on EXTAL is accepted at 40 % to 60 % duty cycle.

Every channel meets the 12-bit single-ended accuracy figures. The conversion clock runs 1 MHz to 18 MHz; the top speed needs CFG2[ADHSC] set and CFG1[ADLPC] cleared, and the lowest power comes from ADLPC set, ADHSC cleared and a 1 MHz clock. The input has RADIN 2 kΩ typ in series and CADIN 4 pF typ; the external source resistance is 5 kΩ max in 12-bit mode below 4 MHz, with RAS × CAS under 1 ns. An on-chip temperature sensor gives 716 mV typ at 25 °C with a 1.62 mV/°C slope.

The CMP has a high-speed mode (PMODE = 1, 50 ns typ, 200 µA max) and a low-speed mode (PMODE = 0, 250 ns typ, 20 µA max), four hysteresis settings from 5 mV to 30 mV typ, and a 6-bit DAC as an internal reference. After a control write it settles within 40 µs.

Program and erase run over the full 1.71 V to 3.6 V supply. A longword programs in 65 µs typ and a sector erases in 14 ms typ. Endurance is 10 K cycles minimum, with 5 years retention after 10 K cycles and 20 years after 1 K cycles.

SPI0 runs as master up to fBUS/2 and as slave up to fBUS/4. I2C meets standard mode (100 kHz) and fast mode (400 kHz); full fast-mode speed at the heaviest bus load needs the high-drive pins, or normal-drive pins with VDD ≥ 2.7 V. The UART and timers follow the general switching figures. The UART0 asynchronous clock may run up to 8 MHz in VLPR and VLPS.
Propagation delays are taken between 50 % points and rise and fall times between 20 % and 80 %. Digital switching figures assume a 30 pF load, slew rate control off and normal drive strength.
Typical figures are at TA = 25 °C and VDD = 3.3 V unless a table gives other conditions; they are neither tested nor guaranteed.
